# Post Asana task updates to Discord

**Pattern:** Event -> route -> notify · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Asana webhook

## What it does
Turns Asana project activity — tasks added, completed, or otherwise changed — into readable Discord messages, each with fitting wording.

## Why it exists
Teams that live in Discord shouldn't have to sit in Asana to know what moved. This pushes task activity into chat in seconds, with the right phrasing for each kind of change.

## Main flow
Asana Project Webhook -> Extract Event & Task -> Route by Event -> Format message -> Post to Discord (failure -> error rail).

## Use it for
- A team that coordinates in Discord but plans in Asana
- Announcing completed tasks without a status meeting
- Read-only project visibility for non-Asana users

## You get
- Asana movement in Discord within seconds
- Fitting wording per event type
- Retried, surfaced failures

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Asana access token; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This is event-driven; sample events (added, completed, other change) are pinned so you can run it with no credential. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Asana access token**
Asana → My Settings → Apps → Manage Developer Apps → Create Personal Access Token. Paste it into n8n's Asana credential.
_Gotcha:_ The token inherits your Asana permissions — it can only read/write projects your own account can see.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**No events arrive**
Cause: The Asana webhook didn't register, or points at the wrong project.
Fix: Asana needs a reachable callback — activate the workflow. Confirm the project GID is the one you mean, not the workspace GID.

**Every change posts as 'changed'**
Cause: Asana events don't always carry a distinct 'added' action for your setup.
Fix: The Switch keys off action/completed; inspect a real event and adjust the rules to match how your project reports changes.

**Discord posts nothing / returns 400**
Cause: The message content resolved to an empty string, or the webhook URL is wrong.
Fix: Discord rejects empty content. Check the upstream expression produced text, and re-copy the webhook URL.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

A Switch (not a chain of IFs) routes the three events because adding a fourth case later is one rule, not another nested branch. The completed case is matched on the task's completed flag rather than the action string, since Asana reports a completion as a 'changed' action with completed=true. Discord runs in webhook mode so nothing has to be installed in the server.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Route different Asana sections to different Discord channels.
2. @mention the new assignee on reassignment by mapping their Asana name to a Discord ID.
3. Suppress notifications for tasks moved to a 'Later' section.
